maria_ops: quick FYI — hit a 401 using REDWOOD_API_KEY I pasted from macOS. I did `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(pbpaste)` and curl -> 401. Local test in iTerm worked tho. anyone seen clipboard/newline weirdness?

kevin_devex: yep, mac paste often includes a trailing newline (
) or CR. try inspecting with xxd: `printf %s "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | xxd` to see hidden chars.

maria_ops: oh nice — xxd shows `0a` at end. so that's probably it. does that break basic auth header building?

alex_platform: can if you base64 the wrong bytes. common mistakes: using `echo` (adds newline) or forgetting the trailing colon when password is empty. recommended: `printf %s "$API_KEY" | base64` (no newline) or explicitly strip newlines first.

toni_sre: also note for Basic auth where username=apikey and password is empty you must include the colon: `username:` before base64. i.e. `printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64` — otherwise server may interpret creds incorrectly.

maria_ops: ok so my repro had two problems — newline from pbpaste and I didn't append `:` in my quick script. current workaround I used: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(pbpaste | tr -d '
')` then `B64=$(printf '%s:' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | base64)` and `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $B64" https://api.redwood.example/v1/` — works now

kevin_devex: :thumbsup: other tips: `echo -n` is not portable (some echos ignore `-n`), so prefer `printf` for scripts. in CI beware Windows runners adding CRLF; use `tr -d ''` if you see `0d` bytes.

alex_platform: node snippet for reference: `const header = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(apiKey + ':').toString('base64')` — easy to forget the `+ ':'`. python: `base64.b64encode((api_key + ':').encode()).decode()`

maria_ops: I'll patch the quickstart and add a macOS clipboard note + a tiny helper: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(pbpaste | tr -d '
')` and a curl example showing the colon.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: staged quickstart doc updated, link: https://docs.redwood.example/devex/quickstart#auth (auto)

toni_sre: one more subtle thing — streaming clients: if the auth header contains a newline some servers will compute content-length differently and drop the connection mid-stream. stripping newline avoids weird intermittent streaming failures.

maria_ops: good call, will mention streaming gotchas too. thanks everyone!

kevin_devex: np — small housekeeping: maybe add a CI check that the sample key in docs has no trailing whitespace (CI linter).

maria_ops: filed a tiny PR to docs and added a line in the SDK FAQ about `printf` vs `echo`. done.
